answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, any delivery disruption is high-stakes right now, and memory_c2 explicitly warns that the low-cost vendor missed SLA in 3 of 4 quarters and should not be sole-sourced for a critical line—ruling out switch_primary_vendor despite the cost pressure. memory_c4 shows that renegotiating at renewal (using market benchmarking) previously recovered real margin and improved payment terms without changing the supply relationship or adding integration/migration risk, which memory_c1 confirms is costly to disturb. Given the 14-day expiry forces action now, and finance needs cost reduction without added delivery risk, negotiating harder terms with the incumbent at renewal is the single decision that addresses the spend mandate while preserving continuity. Adding a second source (memory_c3) or deferring (memory_c5) are both reasonable next-cycle moves but don't fit the urgent 14-day renewal window as directly as renegotiation does, and switching vendors outright contradicts the verified risk record.
